work: Conformal Data Contamination Tests for In-distribution Data Acquisition (Vejling, Pandey, Biscio, Popovski)
venue_status: arXiv 2507.13835 (v1 18 Jul 2025, v2 8 Oct 2026); no venue on page [VERIFY]
setting: A data buyer with local clean data tests K external data agents before acquisition: conformal outlier p-values from a score fitted on local data (split into training and calibration), combined into contamination p-values (Storey, quantile, Fisher, sum) to test H0: contamination factor pi_k <= pi_th; Storey-BH over agents; then data subset selection with BH on row p-values. Experiments: RetinaMNIST vs EyePACS and MNIST (digits 1,4,7) with incorrectly labelled contaminated data
filters: SOURCES (agents) then ROWS (second-stage BH subset selection)

reason: Closest statistical source audit with finite-sample FDR control (Storey-BH). Differences: needs a clean local reference rather than peer comparison; exchangeability fails under drift; an honest-but-different agent is treated as contaminated (category 'honest agents with unintentionally biased data'); no context model, cap or bound. Theorems read concern validity/FDR; I did not locate a power result.
